claims.text: Dynamic amorphization can produce an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface region has a high density of high-angle grain boundaries.
High-angle grain boundaries serve as efficient nucleation pathways for protective oxide formation.
High-angle grain boundaries serve as efficient diffusion pathways during protective oxide formation.
An ultra-nanocrystalline surface produces a more continuous and adherent protective oxide film than a coarse-grained surface.
CoCrFeMnNi can have a single-phase, initially coarse-grained state.
Mechanical stressing can trigger dynamic amorphization and formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
A controlled heat treatment can trigger dynamic amorphization and form an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
Oxidation at 800–1000°C in air is an applicable regime for the proposed grain-boundary-controlled mechanism.
The nanocrystalline grain-boundary network accelerates oxygen diffusion.
Accelerated oxygen diffusion and oxide nucleation lead to rapid growth of a coherent protective oxide film.
The resulting uniform and adherent oxide reduces oxidation rates relative to a coarse-grained surface.
Pre-treated HEAs with ultra-nanocrystalline surfaces will show lower oxidation mass gain than untreated coarse-grained HEAs.
Pre-treated HEAs will form a more continuous, adherent, and slower-growing oxide layer than untreated coarse-grained HEAs.
The mechanism is expected to be significant in single-phase FCC HEAs similar to CoCrFeMnNi.
The stability of the nanocrystalline surface during prolonged high-temperature exposure can affect oxidation outcomes.
